subject: anaesthesia
title: Intraoperative Crises: Bronchospasm, Anaphylaxis, and Venous Air Embolism

steps.title: Intraoperative Bronchospasm Signs
steps.tx: **Acute intraoperative bronchospasm presentation** under general anaesthesia manifests as sudden elevation of peak inspiratory airway pressures with preserved normal plateau pressures (widened peak-to-plateau airway resistance gradient), expiratory musical wheezing on chest auscultation, prolonged expiration, dropping tidal volumes during pressure-controlled ventilation, and a classic upward-sloping 'shark-fin' alveolar plateau (Phase III) on capnography.
steps.say: Acute intraoperative bronchospasm presentation under general anaesthesia manifests as sudden elevation of peak inspiratory airway pressures with preserved normal plateau pressures (widened peak-to-plateau airway resistance gradient), expiratory musical wheezing on chest auscultation, prolonged expiration, dropping tidal volumes during pressure-controlled ventilation, and a classic upward-sloping 'shark-fin' alveolar plateau (Phase III) on capnography.

rows: Check plateau pressure during inspiratory hold
Measure increased alpha angle on tracing
Rule out kinked endotracheal tube or carina carina abutment

steps.tx: Those two traces together point to resistance in the airways rather than a stiff lung. **Acute intraoperative bronchospasm presentation** under general anaesthesia is a sudden rise in peak inspiratory pressure with a preserved normal plateau pressure, so the peak to plateau gap widens. Musical wheeze is heard in expiration, expiration itself is prolonged, and tidal volume falls during pressure controlled ventilation. On capnography, phase III slopes upward into the shark fin alveolar plateau.
steps.say: Intraoperative bronchospasm suddenly raises peak airway pressure while plateau pressure stays normal, widening the gap between them. Expiratory wheeze, a prolonged expiratory phase, and falling tidal volume on pressure controlled breaths occur with an upsloping shark fin on the capnograph. The normal plateau argues against a stiff lung.

steps.title: Immediate Bronchospasm Management
steps.tx: **Emergency treatment of intraoperative bronchospasm** begins with deepening anaesthesia using volatile anaesthetic vapors (sevoflurane or isoflurane act as potent direct bronchodilators) or intravenous propofol/ketamine, while ventilating with 100 percent oxygen. Clinicians must administer inhaled salbutamol (6 to 10 puffs via an in-line MDI adapter), administer intravenous hydrocortisone (100 to 200 mg), and inject subcutaneous or intravenous adrenaline for refractory bronchospasm.

nodes.label: Deepen anaesthesia with 8% sevoflurane or IV propofol bolus
Switch to 100% O2 and adjust ventilator for prolonged expiration
Deliver 8 to 10 puffs of salbutamol via endotracheal in-line spacer
Administer IV magnesium sulphate (2 g) or IV adrenaline for refractory spasm

steps.title: Perioperative Anaphylaxis Triggers
steps.tx: **Etiology of perioperative anaphylaxis** identifies neuromuscular blocking agents (specifically rocuronium and succinylcholine, possessing immunogenic tertiary and quaternary ammonium epitopes) as the primary cause in over 60 percent of cases, followed by intravenous antibiotics (penicillins and cephalosporins in 15 to 20 percent), natural rubber latex, chlorhexidine skin prep, and intravenous colloidal volume expanders.
steps.say: Etiology of perioperative anaphylaxis identifies neuromuscular blocking agents (specifically rocuronium and succinylcholine, possessing immunogenic tertiary and quaternary ammonium epitopes) as the primary cause in over 60 percent of cases, followed by intravenous antibiotics (penicillins and cephalosporins in 15 to 20 percent), natural rubber latex, chlorhexidine skin prep, and intravenous colloidal volume expanders.

rows: High cross-reactivity across all muscle relaxants
Sensitization via central line insertion dressings
Severe allergy in spina bifida and healthcare workers

steps.tx: The tryptase sample can wait. The circulation cannot. In perioperative **anaphylaxis** the trigger, often a neuromuscular blocker or an antibiotic just given, is stopped, and adrenaline is titrated in small intravenous boluses through the cannula already in place. If there is no intravenous access, 0.5 milligrams goes into muscle. A crystalloid bolus is run quickly, because vasodilatation has emptied the venous return. Antihistamine and steroid are adjuncts. They do not stand in for the adrenaline.
steps.say: Perioperative anaphylaxis is treated with titrated adrenaline and a fast fluid bolus, and the likely trigger infusion is stopped. Chlorphenamine and hydrocortisone do not replace adrenaline.

vis.alt: Resuscitation algorithm for perioperative anaphylaxis, with adrenaline titration and intravenous fluid.
vis.caption: The anaphylaxis path gives adrenaline, titrated to the blood pressure, together with a rapid fluid bolus. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Anaphylaxis Presentation and Grading
steps.tx: **Clinical presentation of anaesthetic anaphylaxis** is often masked by surgical drapes: the earliest and most dramatic sign is sudden, unexplained cardiovascular collapse with profound hypotension, accompanied by severe bronchospasm with high airway pressures. Cutaneous signs (generalized erythema, urticaria, angioedema) are absent in up to 30 percent of severe cases until circulation is resuscitated.

left.title: Severe Cardiovascular Collapse
points: Profound, refractory hypotension and absent peripheral pulses
Massive systemic vasodilation and increased capillary permeability
Loss of up to 40 to 50 percent of intravascular volume into interstitium

right.title: Respiratory and Cutaneous Manifestations
points: Acute severe bronchospasm with unventilatable lungs
Urticaria, flushing, and wheals frequently hidden under drapes

steps.title: Adrenaline First-Line Therapy
steps.tx: **Adrenaline administration in perioperative anaphylaxis** represents the non-negotiable first-line drug: adrenaline acts as an alpha-1 agonist to restore vascular tone and blood pressure, a beta-1 agonist to augment myocardial contractility, and a beta-2 agonist to relax bronchial smooth muscle and halt further mast cell mediator degranulation. Titrate intravenous boluses of 50 to 100 micrograms (0.5 to 1 mL of 1:10,000 solution) every 1 to 2 minutes.

Titrate intravenous boluses of 50 to 100 micrograms (0.5 to 1 mL of 1:10,000 solution) every 1 to 2 minutes.

nodes.label: Halt all potential allergens and discontinue volatile anaesthetics
Administer immediate IV adrenaline bolus 50 to 100 micrograms
Infuse rapid crystalloid fluid bolus (20 to 40 mL/kg)
Start continuous IV adrenaline infusion (0.05-0.2 mcg/kg/min) for shock

steps.title: Diagnostic Serum Mast Cell Tryptase
steps.tx: **Diagnostic serum mast cell tryptase timing** confirms an IgE-mediated immunological reaction: draw baseline clotted blood for total tryptase immediately during initial resuscitation (within 1 to 2 hours of symptom onset), draw a second sample at 2 to 4 hours post-reaction, and draw a convalescent baseline sample at 24 hours. A peak tryptase exceeding 1.2 times baseline plus 2 micrograms per liter establishes anaphylaxis.

rows: Reflects acute mast cell degranulation surge
Draw alongside acute arterial blood gases
Guides necessity of intensive care monitoring
Essential reference for definitive formula calculation
Essential before any future general anaesthesia

steps.title: Venous Air Embolism Mechanics
steps.tx: **Venous air embolism pathogenesis** occurs when a negative pressure gradient develops between an open non-collapsible venous lumen and the atmosphere, classically during sitting craniotomy, posterior cervical spine surgery, or central venous cannulation. Air entering the right atrium forms an air-lock obstruction in the right ventricular outflow tract, triggering acute cor pulmonale, hypoxaemia, and sudden drops in end-tidal carbon dioxide.

left.title: Monitoring Sensitivity Spectrum
points: Transoesophageal echocardiography (TOE) is most sensitive (0.02 mL/kg)
Precordial Doppler detects air bubbles as churning washing-machine sounds
Sudden steep drop in end-tidal CO2 reflects pulmonary vascular obstruction

right.title: Emergency Treatment Actions
points: Flood surgical field with saline and occlude open venous bone sinuses
Position patient in Durant position (left lateral decubitus, Trendelenburg)
Aspirate air from right atrium via multiorifice central venous catheter

steps.title: Intraoperative Hypoxia DOPE Algorithm
steps.tx: **Intraoperative hypoxia DOPE algorithm** rapidly evaluates acute respiratory desaturation under general anaesthesia: Dislodgement of the endotracheal tube (accidental extubation or right mainstem endobronchial intubation), Obstruction of the tube (secretions, biting, blood, kinking), Pneumothorax (tension pneumothorax with absent breath sounds and hypotension), and Equipment failure (ventilator disconnect, oxygen supply failure).

nodes.label: Dislodgement: check tube depth and bilateral breath sounds
Obstruction: pass suction catheter down tube lumen to carina
Pneumothorax: auscultate chest, check tracheal deviation and peak pressures
Equipment: switch to manual Ambu bag with 100% cylinder O2
